title: Data Lineage & Privacy: Handling GDPR Deletions in Data Cloud

steps.prompt: A customer submits a GDPR "Right to be Forgotten" erasure request. How must an architect ensure complete erasure compliance across Data Cloud and connected source systems?

options.label: Execute the Data Cloud Consent API (Data Subject Rights / Forget Me request), which purges customer records across DLOs, unified DMOs, and calculated insights
options.rationale: The Data Cloud Consent API coordinates cryptographic erasure across both raw storage and unified model layers, ensuring global regulatory compliance.

options.label: Delete the record in core CRM and assume Data Cloud will auto-delete it during the next sync
options.distractorAntipattern: Data Cloud retains historic DLO snapshots unless Consent API is invoked.
options.rationale: Source deletions do not automatically purge historical immutable data lake storage without explicit Data Subject Rights requests.

options.label: Change the customer name to "Deleted User" in the CRM UI
options.distractorAntipattern: UI pseudonymization leaves unmasked data in underlying lakehouse storage.
options.rationale: Superficial field editing leaves PII unmasked across data lake storage, violating GDPR audit requirements.
